rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Receiving the record in the left hand humiliates the sinner: his left hand is twisted behind his back to take it, exposing his ugly deeds.
rows.anchor: {وأما من أوتى كتابه بشماله} تحقيرا له لأن الشمال يتشاءم بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His words express grief, regret, and fear; this spiritual pain is more severe than bodily pain.
rows.anchor: تحزنا وتحسرا وخوفا مما فيه وهو من قبيل الألم الروحاني الذي هو أشد من الألم الجسمني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive form means that he was not given the record.
rows.anchor: مجهول منا لإيتاء بمعنى لم أعط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He calls it his book because it has gathered all his evil deeds.
rows.anchor: هذا الذي جمع جميع سيئاتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: درى here means to know; after seeing the bad outcome, he wishes he had not known his reckoning.
rows.anchor: متكلم من الدراية بمعنى العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما may be interrogative, suspending the verb from taking its object, or relative with an implied subject in its clause.
rows.anchor: فما استفهامية معلق بها الفعل عن العلم ويجوز أن تكون موصولة بتقدير المبتدأ في الصلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated wish renews his regret; he wishes his first death, implicit in context, had ended his life so he would not be resurrected or face this shame.
rows.anchor: يا ليتها} تكرير للتمني وتجديد للتحسر أي يا ليت الموتة التي متها وذقتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, يا ليتها refers to the present ordeal: he wishes this state had been the death that ended life, since he now finds it worse than death, though he hated death in life.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ضمير ليتها لما شاهد من الحالة أي يا ليت هذه الحالة كانت الموتة

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: The cited poet illustrates that one may wish for death when an experience is worse than death, even though death is itself the greatest calamity.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر : وشر من الموت الذي إن لقيته تمنيت منه الموت والموت أعظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the negative reading, the phrase means that the wealth did not ward off any of the afterlife's punishment; the object is omitted.
rows.anchor: أيلم يدفع عني شيئا من عذاب الآخرة على أن ما نافية والمفعول محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the relative reading, ماليه includes worldly wealth and followers; the prepositional lām attached to the possessive yā broadens the reference.
rows.anchor: المال والاتباع على أن ما موصولة واللام جارة داخلة على ياء المتكلم ليعم مثل الاتباع

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf takes the wording as both negation and a rhetorical question of denial: what did his worldly means avail him?
rows.anchor: الكشاف" ما أغنى نفي واستفهام على وجه الإنكار أي أي شيء أغنى عني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent meaning is his worldly money alone: it distracted and harmed him instead of helping, as in the cited verses about wealth failing its owner.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أن مالية هو المال المضاف إلى ياء المتكلم أي لم يغن عني المال الذي جمعته في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects the majority exegetical generalization to wealth and followers as departing from the Quran's apparent wording.
rows.anchor: فما ذهب إليه أكثر أهل التفسير من التعميم عدول عما ورد به ظاهر القرآن

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib derives sultan from mastery by force; it can denote power, its possessor, or an argument, whose force reaches hearts, especially those of learned believers.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب السلاطة التمكن من القهر ومنه سمى السلطان والسلطان يقال في السلاطة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading is that his kingship and control over people have vanished, leaving him poor and humiliated.
rows.anchor: ملكي وتسلطي على الناس وبقيت فقيرا ذليلا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the lost sultan as the argument the speaker used to make against others in worldly life, now rendered void.
rows.anchor: كما روى عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما ومعناه بطلت هجتي التي كنت أحتج بها عليهم في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument reading is more fitting because receiving the record in the left hand applies to all the wretched, not only kings.
rows.anchor: ورجح هذا المعنى بأن من أوتى كتابه بشماله لا اختصاص له بالملوك بل هو عام لجميع أهل الشقاوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wealth wording alludes to wealthy Quraysh leaders such as al-Walid, while the mention of lost power exposes their worldly status.
rows.anchor: يدل على الأول على أن فيه تعريضا بنحو الوليد من رؤساء قريش وأهل ثروتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lost sultan may also mean losing command over one's powers, faculties, and limbs, which one can no longer employ in worship at resurrection.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المنى تسلطي على القوى والآلات فعجزت عن استمالها في العبادات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is God's order to the keepers of the Fire, the zabāniya, to seize the disobedient man whose record was given in his left hand.
rows.anchor: حكاية لما يقول الله يومئذ لخزنة النار وهمالزبانية الموكلون على عذابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without delay, they gather his hands to his neck and bind them with an iron collar.
rows.anchor: بلا مهلة أي أجمعوا يديه إلى عنقه بالقيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ghull is an iron neck ring joining hand to neck and restricting head movement; the word describes placing such a restraint on someone.
rows.anchor: يقال غل فلان وضع في عنقه أو يده الغل وهو بالضم الطوق من حديد الجامع لليد إلى العنق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting a neck collar on a slave is disliked because it is a punishment of the people of Hell.
rows.anchor: وفي الفقه وكره جعل الغل في عنق عبده لأنه عقوبة أهل النار

rows.speaker: الفقيه
rows.claim: A jurist says collars were customary in his time when flight was feared; unlike shackling, they are not disliked in that case, while restraint is Muslim practice for rebels.
rows.anchor: وقال الفقيه إن في زماننا جرت العادة بذلك إذا خيف من الأباق كمال في الكبرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting al-jahim restricts the burning: admit and burn him only in the great Fire, fitting punishment for his arrogance.
rows.anchor: دل التقديم على التخصيص والمعنى لا تصلوه أي لا تدخلوه إلا الجحيم

rows.speaker: سعدى المفتي
rows.claim: Saʿdi al-Mufti infers that the restriction applies specifically to the arrogant, because the condemned man had exalted himself over people.
rows.anchor: قال سعدى المفتي فيكون مخصوصا بالمتعظمين وفيه بحث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chain is made of fire, with linked rings; its length is seventy cubits.
rows.anchor: وهي حلق منتظمة كل حلقة منها في حلقة والجار متعلق بقوله فاسلكوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ذرعها means its length; a cubit is the measure taken by the arm or an iron rod or stick.
rows.anchor: الذراع ككتاب ما يذرع به حديدا أو قضيبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ذرعها is the subject, سبعون is its predicate, the clause modifies سلسلة, and ذراعا is a specification.
rows.anchor: والجملة في محل الجر على إنها صفة سلسلة وقوله {ذراعا} تمييز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salk means to insert something into a path, thread, or restraint; they wrap the chain around his body, enclosing and constricting him.
rows.anchor: السلك هو زدخال في الطريق والخيط والقيد وغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated ثم marks increasing terror among binding, roasting, and chain punishment, not elapsed time; the scene's threat requires no pause between torments.
rows.anchor: ثم الدلالة على تفاوت ما بين العذابين الغل وتسلية الجحيم

rows.speaker: ابن الشيخ
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh avoids coordinating both ثم and ف on one clause by positing omitted successive commands to the wardens; ثم links the commands, while ف signals immediate execution.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الشيخ إن كلمتي ثم والقاء إن كانتا لعطف جملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-muhl here may be iron slag melted gradually or thick oil dregs flowing slowly.
rows.anchor: وهو ههنا خبث الحديد ونوه مما يذاب على مهل وتدريج أودردى الزيت لسيلانه على مهل

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud compares the sky to molten silver for its changing colors, or to pitch and tar for their blackness.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود كالفضة المذابة في تلونها أو كالقير والقطران في سوادهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يوم may attach to قريبا, meaning the event is possible and will be manifest that day, or to an implied clause that such indescribable terrors occur then.
rows.anchor: ويوم متعلق بقريبا أي يمكن ولا يتعذر في ذلك اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عهن is dyed wool; when shattered and scattered in the air, the differently colored mountains resemble wool blown by wind.
rows.anchor: العهن الصوف المصبوغ قال تعالى

rows.speaker: كشف الأسرار
rows.claim: Kashf al-Asrar gives a three-stage transformation: mountains first become shifting sand, then carded wool, then scattered particles.
rows.anchor: قال في كشف الأسرار أول ما تنغير الجبال تصير رملا مهيلا ثم عهنا منفوشا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No close friend or relative asks another about their condition or speaks to them, because each is occupied by their own ordeal; if relatives do not, strangers certainly will not.
rows.anchor: أي لا يسأل قريب قريبا عن أحواله ولا يكلمه لابتلاء كل منهم بما شغله عن ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite wording generalizes the scene to every close-friend pair.
rows.anchor: وإذا كان الحال بين الأقارب هكذا فكيف يكون بين الأجانب والتنكير للتعميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause answers an implied objection: perhaps they do not ask because they cannot see one another; they do see each other.
rows.anchor: أنه قيل لعله لا يبصره فكيف يسأل عن حاله فقل يصبرونهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first pronoun refers to the first close friend and the second to the other; both are plural to generalize across all pairs.
rows.anchor: والضمير الأول لحميم أول والثاني للثاني وجمع الضميرين لعموم الحميم لكل حميمين

rows.speaker: تاج المصادر
rows.claim: Taj al-Masadir glosses tabṣir as making something clear or evident; the verb can take its second object with bi, which may be omitted here.
rows.anchor: قال في تاج المصادر التبصير بينا كردن.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fasila originally means a piece separated from a body; it can denote close forebears or children, since a child is separated from its parents and they from it.
rows.anchor: وهي في الأصل القطعة المفصولة من الجسد وتطلق على الآباء الأقربين وعلى الأولاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here fasila means the nearest forebears and clan, as confirmed by the preceding mention of his children.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالفصيلة في الآية هو الآباء الأقربون والعشيرة الأدنون لقوله وبنيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To shelter someone is to draw them near or gather them in; his kin either include him by lineage or shelter him in adversity.
rows.anchor: أوى إلى كذا انضم إليه وآواه غيره كما قال تعالى آوى إليه أخاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This includes all creatures, jinn and humankind; the masculine من is used by semantic predominance.
rows.anchor: من الثقلين والخلائق ومن للتغليب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause coordinates with يفتدي; ثم signals how unlikely rescue would be, even after he offers everyone on earth as ransom.
rows.anchor: عطف على يفتدى أي يود لو يفدتى ثم ينجيه الافتداء وثم لاستبعاد الإنجاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The criminal would wish to ransom himself with all his family and every creature, yet such a ransom cannot save him.
rows.anchor: يتمنى لو كان هؤلاء جميعا تحت يده وبذلهم في فداء نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul stained by the lower self would ransom itself from separation and veiling with heart's children and qualities, its companion self, secret's brother, followers, and all spiritual and bodily powers; ruined readiness and lost time make this futile.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى مجرم الروح المنصبغ بصبغة النفس فإنه يود أن يفتدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كلا rebukes the wish and declares rescue impossible: the criminal's darkened condition through sin has earned punishment.
rows.anchor: ردع للمجرم عن الودادة وتصريح بامتناع إنجاء الافتداء أي لا يكون كما يتمنى

rows.speaker: القرطبي
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi allows كلا to mean either rebuke or indeed; on the latter reading, ينجيه closes the preceding sentence and كلا starts the next.
rows.anchor: وعن القرطبي أن كلا يكون بمعنى الردع وبمعنى حقا وكلا الوجهين جائز

rows.speaker: المحققون
rows.claim: The authorities and the Sajawandi stopping mark favor the rebuke reading, placing an unrestricted pause at كلا.
rows.anchor: والمحققون على الأول ومن ذلك وضع السجاوندي علامة الوقف المطلق على كلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to Hell, indicated by the preceding mention of punishment.
rows.anchor: أي النار المدلول عليها بذكر العذاب والمراد جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laza is a name for the Fire or its second level, derived from a pure, smokeless flame; alternatively it means such a flame directly and denotes extreme burning.
rows.anchor: وهو علم للنار وللدرك الثاني منها منقول من اللظى بمعنى الهب الخالص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nazaʿ means to pull something from its place and tear it away; shawa can mean the nonfatal extremities such as hands and feet.
rows.anchor: نزع الشيء جذبه من مقره وقلعه والشوى الأطراف أي الأعضاء التي ليست بمقتل كالأيدي والأرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intensive form is used for terror: the fiercely hot Fire tears away extremities, then restores them so the torment repeats forever.
rows.anchor: ونزاعة على الاختصاص للتهويل أي أعني بلظى جذابة للأعضاء الواقعة في أطراف الجسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shawa may also mean the scalp's skin: the Fire strips the head, matching the sinners' use of their limbs to harm and their failure to use reason for truth.
rows.anchor: والشوى جمع شواة وهي جلدة الرأس يعني أن النار تنزع جلود الرأس وتقشر عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who turn away from truth and its recognition are drawn to the Fire and brought into it; calling them is a metaphor for bringing them present.
rows.anchor: أي عن الحق ومعرفته وهو مقابل أقبل ومعنى تدعو تجذب إلى نفسها وتحضر

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: The Najmiyya interpretation takes turning back as failure to face God through obedience to the law and resistance to the lower nature.
rows.anchor: وفي التأويلات النجمية : من أدبر عن التوجه إلى الحق بموافقات الشريعة ومخالفات الطبيعة

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: It reads turning away as abandoning the approach to the afterlife and the turning away from worldly life.
rows.anchor: وتولى عن الإقبال على الآخرة والإدبار عن الدنيا

rows.speaker: القاشاني
rows.claim: Al-Qashani says like inclines to like: the Fire of lower nature summons those who turn from truth and the holy realm, face darkness, and love transient lower things, drawing them by natural affinity.
rows.anchor: وقال القاشاني : بمناسبة نفسه للجحيم أنجر إليها إذ الجنس إلى الجنس يميل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fire may call sinners aloud by their names and seize them like a bird picking up grain.
rows.anchor: أو تدعو الكافرين والمنافقين بلفظ فصيح بأسمائهم ثم تلقتطهم كالتقاط الطير الحبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God creates speech in the Fire as He does in human skin and limbs or in a tree, enabling it to call the sinners.
rows.anchor: ويجوز يخلق الله فيها كلاما كما يخلقه في جلودهم وأيديهم وأرجلهم وكما خلقه في الشجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the Fire calls its keepers with an omitted possessive, or the verb is figuratively attributed to the Fire as the destination called toward.
rows.anchor: أو تدعو زبانيتها على حذف المضاف أو على الإسناد المجازي حيث أسند فعل الداعي إلى المدعو إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sura al-Jinn is Makkan and consists of twenty-eight verses.
rows.anchor: ثمان وعشرون آية مكية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is addressed to Muhammad, telling him to convey this to his people.
rows.anchor: يا محمد لقومك {أوحى إلى} أي ألقى على بطريق الوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waḥy means a hidden communication or report from God; disclosing this news shows Muhammad is messenger to both jinn and humankind, forbids shirk, and urges tawhid.
rows.anchor: ألقى على بطريق الوحي وأخبرت بأعلام من الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening أنَّه is accusative as the subject of أوحي, and its pronoun refers to the matter or affair being reported.
rows.anchor: بالفتح لأنه فاعل أوحى والضمير الشأن أي أن الشأن والحديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of استمع is omitted and may be Qur'an, Ṭā Hā, or اقرأ, understood from what follows.
rows.anchor: أي القرآن أو طه أو اقرأ وقد حذف لدلالة ما بعده عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An attentive listener intentionally listens; a hearer may catch sound without intending to, so every listener hears but not every hearer listens.
rows.anchor: والمستمع من كان قاصدا للسماع مصغيا إليه والسامع من اتفق سماعه من غير قصد إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafar means a group of jinn numbering more than three but fewer than ten.
rows.anchor: {نفر من الجن} جماعة منهم

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: Al-Qamus defines nafar as fewer than ten men and gives anfār as its plural.
rows.anchor: قال في "القاموس" : النفر ما دون العشرة من الرجال كالنفير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that at Fajr in Nakhlah, while Muhammad and companions prayed after traveling toward Ukaz, passing jinn heard the Quran and listened; the Prophet neither saw nor knew them, nor had recited to them deliberately, and learned of them by revelation.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما انطلق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في طائفة من أصحابه إلى سوق عكاظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jinn are subtle bodies in forms unlike angels and humans, ordinarily hidden from human sight; they can address miracle workers and whisper to other people.
rows.anchor: والجن أجسام رقاق فيصورة تخالف صورة الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jinn are predominantly fiery or airy; the author cites the Quran's creation of jinn from a smokeless flame and explains beings by whichever of the four elements predominates.
rows.anchor: يغلب عليهم النارية أو الهوائية ويدل على الأول مثل قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most philosophers deny that jinn exist externally, while many ancient philosophers and most religious communities affirm their existence.
rows.anchor: وأكثر الفلاسفة ينكرون وجود الجن في الخارج واعترف به جمع عظيم من قدمائهم وكذا جمهور أرباب الملل

rows.speaker: القاشاني
rows.claim: Al-Qashani describes jinn as earthly souls less dense than animal natures yet unlike human or pure spiritual souls, attached to subtle airy, fiery, or smoky elemental forms called suspended images by some philosophers.
rows.anchor: قال القاشاني : إن في الوجود نفوسا أرضية قوية لا في غلظ التقوس السبعية والبهيمة

rows.speaker: القاشاني
rows.claim: Al-Qashani says jinn have cognitions like ours and, being near the heavenly realm, can receive some unseen knowledge and ascend to overhear angels, understood as disembodied souls.
rows.anchor: أمكنها أن تتلقى من عالمه بعض الغيب فلا يستبعد أن ترتقى أفق السماء فتسترق السمع من كلام الملائكة

rows.speaker: القاشاني
rows.claim: Despite their earthly weakness, heavenly forces repel them from higher knowledge; smoky bodies may ignite under stars' rays and perish or be driven back down, possibilities confirmed by truthful prophets and saints.
rows.anchor: ولما كان أرضية ضعيفة بالنسبة إلى القوى السماوية تأثرت تلك القوى فرجمت بتأثيرها عن بلوغ شأوها

rows.speaker: القاشاني
rows.claim: Al-Qashani locates jinn within human existence too, concealed in the unseen inward realm.
rows.anchor: وهي في الوجود الإنساني لاستتارها في غيب الباطن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jinn spoke these words to their own people when they returned to them.
rows.anchor: فقالوا} لقومهم عند رجوعهم إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They call it a Quran because it is a book recited on the Messenger's tongue.
rows.anchor: قرءانا} أي كتابا مقروأ على لسان الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verbal noun عجَب is used adjectivally for emphasis; the Quran is wondrous because it exceeds familiar likenesses and human speech in arrangement and subtle meaning.
rows.anchor: مصدر بمعنى العجيب وضع موضعه للمبالغة والعجيب ما خرج

rows.speaker: البقلي
rows.claim: Al-Baqli calls it a wondrous, astonishing book and infers that the jinn were people of eloquent language.
rows.anchor: وقال البقلي كتابا عجيبا تكربه وفيه إشارة إلى أنهم كانوا من أهل اللسان

rows.speaker: عيزار بن حريث
rows.claim: At Ibn Masud's gathering, a traveler related that he and companions buried a wounded snake; two jinn women later identified it as Amr, the last of those who heard the Prophet's Quran, killed in fighting between believing and unbelieving jinn. They offered compensation, but the men had acted without seeking worldly return; they praised them. The snake-wrapper was Safwan ibn Muattal al-Muradi.
rows.anchor: قال عيزارين حريث كنت عند عبد الله بن مسعود رضي الله عنه فأتاه رجل فقال له كنا في سفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran guides to truth, sound judgment, and the good of religion and worldly life, including tawhid and transcendence; faith in it entails faith in the messenger who brought it.
rows.anchor: إلى الحق والصواب وصلاح الدين والدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's supplication, اللهم ألهمني رشدي, uses rushd for guidance to one's religious and worldly interests.
rows.anchor: كما قال عليه السلام اللهم ألهمني رشدي أي الاهتداء إلى مصالح الدين والدنيا

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some distinguish rushd, like قفل, as the opposite of misguidance in worldly and afterlife matters, from rashad, like ذهب, reserved for afterlife matters.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم الرشد كالقفل خلاف الغي يقال في الأمور الدنيوية والأخروية والرشد كالذهب يقال في الأمور الأخروية فقط

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the true meaning of rushd is arrival at God.
rows.anchor: وحقيقة الرشد هو الوصول إلى الله تعالى قال بعضهم الرشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise of abundant water indicates that jinn eat and drink, though the author says the details were discussed earlier.
rows.anchor: وفيه دلالة على أن الجن يأكلون ويشربون وليكن فيه تفصيل وقد سبق

rows.speaker: بعض أهل المعرفة
rows.claim: Some people of spiritual knowledge read steadfastness on the path as following the Sunna and inclining toward the righteous; watering means pouring affection onto their hearts.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض أهل المعرفة المراد بالاستقامة على الطريقة هو القيام على سبيل السنة والميل إلى أهل الصلاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The test may concern their gratitude for abundant provision or be a test through the water itself; both readings lead to the same result.
rows.anchor: لتختبرهم في ذلك الإسقاء والتوسيع كيف يشكرونه

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kashifi says God gives them a long life so they fulfil the duties of gratitude.
rows.anchor: وقال الكاشفي) تبيارز ماييم ايشانرادر آن زندكانى كه بوظائف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those given spiritual provision and meaningful nourishment must give thanks through obedience, worship, and service.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن المرزوق بالرزق الروحاني والغذاء المعنوي يجب عليه القيام بشكره أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning from remembrance may mean turning from God's worship, admonition, or revelation.
rows.anchor: عن عبادته أو عن موعظته أو وحيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God inserts the offender into a hard, arduous punishment that rises and overwhelms him; صعد is a verbal noun used adjectivally.
rows.anchor: أي شاقا صعبا يتصعد أي يعلوا لمعذب ويغلبه فلا يطيقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salk means insertion, as threading something through an eye; the preposition is omitted as in the question about what led people into Saqar.
rows.anchor: يقال سلكت الخيط في الأبرة إذا أدخلته فيها أي يسلكه في عذاب صعد كما قال ما سلككم في سقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If turning away means disbelief, the punishment is eternal; otherwise it lasts according to the sin unless God forgives it.
rows.anchor: إن كان إعراضه بعدم التصديق عذابه بالتأبيد وإلا فبقدر جريمته إن لم يغفر له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report describes Ṣaʿad as a Hell mountain on which hands and feet melt when placed and are restored when lifted.
rows.anchor: وروى إن صعدا جبل في النار إذا وضع عليه يديه أو رجليه ذابتا وإذا رفعهما عادتا

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another report calls it a smooth Hell mountain; al-Walid ibn al-Mughira is made to climb for forty years, then dragged down in chains and made to repeat the climb forever.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : صعدا جبل أملس في جهنم ويكلف الوليد ابن المغيرة صعوده أربعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is another item revealed, coordinated with the opening revelation that the jinn listened; the mosques belong to God for worship, especially the Sacred Mosque, hence Bayt Allah.
rows.anchor: عطف على قوله إنه استمتع أي وأوحى إلى إن المساجد مختصة بالله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mosques include places built for prayer and remembrance, including the worship houses of other religious communities such as churches and synagogues.
rows.anchor: فالمراد بالمساجد المواضع التي بنيت للصلاة وذكر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing a mosque to a person or place does not contradict its belonging to God: such names may indicate its builder or location.
rows.anchor: ثم هذا لا ينافي أن تضاف المساجد وتنسب إلى غيره تعالى بوجه آخر إما لبانيها كمسجد رسول الله أو لمكانها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hierarchy of sanctity runs from the Sacred Mosque to the Prophet's Mosque, Jerusalem, congregational mosques, neighborhood mosques, street mosques, and home mosques.
rows.anchor: وأعظم المساجد حرمة المسجد الحرام ثم مسجد المدينة ثم مسجد بيت القمدس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The causal fa prohibits worshipping anyone alongside God in mosques; if associating partners is blameworthy, directing worship exclusively to another is worse.
rows.anchor: أي لا تعبدوا فيها الفاء للسببية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mosques of the heart should be purified for the manifestation of God's Greatest Name alone, with no partial names beside it.
rows.anchor: فلا تدعوا مع الله أحا من الأسماء الجزئية أي طهروا مساجد قلوبكم لتجلي اسم الله الأعظم فيها لا غير

rows.speaker: ابن عطاء
rows.claim: Ibn Ata calls the mosques the body's prostrating limbs—face, hands, knees, and feet—and says they must not be humbled before anything but their Creator.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء مساجدك أعضاؤك التي أمرت أن تسجد عليها لا تخضعها ولا تذللها لغير خالقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These limbs drive movement and action, through which sins and desires are pursued; prostrating with them atones, erases sin, and purifies.
rows.anchor: إن هذه الأعضاء التي عليها مدار الحركة هي المفاصل التي تنفتح وتنطبق في المشي والبطش وأكثر السعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is another part of what was revealed: that the matter was so when God's servant stood.
rows.anchor: من جملة الموحى به أي وأوحى إلى أن الشأن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abd Allah refers to the Prophet, counted among his names because he is the true servant, joined to the Greatest Name distinctly while manifesting it comprehensively.
rows.anchor: إلى النبي عليه السلام ولذا جعلوا في أسمائه لأنه هو العبد الحقيقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tradition says the Prophet liked no name more than Abd Allah; his perfect station in servitude could not be matched by others.
rows.anchor: آن حضرت را عليه السلام هي نام ارين خوشتر نيامده ه شريطه عادت وعبوديت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran calls him God's servant in the Night Journey and in the revelation of the Criterion, linking the name to his ascent and receiving revelation.
rows.anchor: تبارك الذي نزل الفرقان على عبده

rows.speaker: شاعر
rows.claim: The cited Persian couplet praises God's servant as marked by beloved servitude, whose path through bondage is unknown to kings.
rows.anchor: آن بنده شعار بندكى دوست كزجمله بندكان كزين اوست داند ببند كيش راهى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling him the servant highlights the cause of his standing and worship—his servanthood—and expresses humility, as though he said, God revealed that when I stood.
rows.anchor: وإيراده عليه السلام بلفظ العبد للإشعار بما هو المقتضي لقيامه وعبادته وهو العبودية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the accusative reading, the clause can be understood as the Prophet speaking of himself; on Nafi and Abu Bakr's reading, Abd Allah must signal the cause of his standing.
rows.anchor: وهذا على قراءة الفتح وإما على قراءة نافع وأبي بكر فيتعين كونه للإشعار بالمقتضى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is circumstantial of the one who stood: he was worshipping God, in the Fajr prayer at Nakhlah described earlier.
rows.anchor: حال من فاعل قام أي يعبده وذلك قيامه لصلاة الفجر بنخلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the accusative reading, كادوا refers to the jinn, who crowded over Muhammad in amazement at his worship and Quran and imitated his companions' prayer postures.
rows.anchor: أي قرب الجن {يكونون عليه لبدا} جمع لبدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Libad is the plural of libda: things piled and stuck together, like a lion's mane; here it describes a dense crowd.
rows.anchor: وهي ما تلبد بعضه على بعض أي تراكب وتلاصق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the genitive reading, if the phrase is the jinn's speech, كادوا instead refers to Muhammad's companions following him in prayer.
rows.anchor: وعلى قراءة الكسر إذا جعل مقول الجن فضمير كادوا لأصحابه عليه السلام الذين كانوا مقتدين به في الصلاة
